scope: Narrow read-only consistency review of introductory survival-conditioned BC/H definitions and the Doob explanation; existing conditioned-survival equations, proof, assumptions, and protected equation aliases.
findings: Surv is terminal ordinary-state arrival, equivalent to never entering the cemetery because the established kernels absorb there. Z_M and the conditioned path laws are defined before the new BC_surv/H_surv names.

Strict positivity Z_A,Z_B>0 is retained explicitly in the preceding definition and governs the conditioned laws used by the following theorem; it was moved, not dropped. Normalizing each complete path law by its own Z_M gives normalized probabilities and H_surv^2=1-BC_surv.

The remaining-survival function is interpreted through continuation from a state, including unreachable states, preserving the intended meaning of the conditional-probability notation on null marginal events.

The Doob quotient is asserted on positive-survival rows only. The survival averaging identity gives row sums one; its nonnegative probabilities give nonnegative entries. Arbitrary normalized completion of zero-survival rows remains valid because conditioned trajectories cannot reach them.
The conditioned geometric-kernel quotient retains the joint-positive denominator condition. All post-hoc normalization formulas and terminal-map statements are unchanged.

Levin and Peres, Section 17.6.1, supports the harmonic reweighting, stochastic row calculation, and conditioning interpretation. The layered survival recurrence is the corresponding finite-horizon instance.
The protected conditioned-bc-kernel alias still specializes the identical generic path-overlap formula to conditioned kernels, with the distinct survival proof and physical witnesses retained.

latest_prose_review.doob_clarification: h is now explicitly a nonnegative state function, specialized to the remaining survival probability psi in [0,1]. Ordinary layer-0 terminal states retain the general Markov scope; a separate sentence identifies inputs in the attribution application. The positive-source quotient, weighted-average row normalization, and Bayes interpretation are correct. Existing positivity and zero-survival completion assumptions are unchanged.
construction_comparison: Algebraic proximity to local maxima is justified by max(a-b,c-d)=max(a+d,c+b)-(b+d); the ReLU pair is the case c=d=0. The local-maxima minimum identity uses the same common-term/max algebra. No equality with either global algorithm is claimed.
The absolute-curvature scalar construction has p_second=(f_second)_positive and q_second=(f_second)_negative almost everywhere, matching the one-dimensional positive/negative-fold interpretation.

Representation dependence is substantive: applying the layerwise recursion to ReLU(-ReLU(u-v)) yields the identical pair (max(u,v),max(u,v)) for the zero function, whereas either global construction applied to the zero function yields (0,0). This validates the retained caveat.
latest_prose_review.resolved_precision: Changed ordinary input state to ordinary terminal state at layer 0 before final hash binding; retained a separate attribution interpretation.
